item: Victorian brown transfer-printed ironstone dinner service in the 'Sydney' pattern (urn with flowers and a ewer in the centre, Greek-key/shell-and-anthemion border). Backstamp reads SYDNEY in an octagonal cartouche with a pattern letter. Per a Casey & Lowe ceramic report, 'Sydney' is one of four transfer patterns (Chantilly, Corsina, Sydenham, Sydney) attributed to John Thomson (& Sons), Glasgow Scotland, so likely Scottish export ware of c.1860s-80s that sold into Australia. Owner's handwritten note: Brown Transfer Dinner Set, 6 dinner plates, 9 B/B (bread and butter) plates, 7 soup plates, 1 medium serving platter, 1 small platter (23 pieces).
note: Antique pair, Georgian/19thC brown transferware mourning plates (older, different pattern); excludes postage
